meta.important_question: Does credible evidence emerge that fellowship delays were intentionally used to discourage union organizing?

endpoint_ledger.rationale: This is the core factual endpoint underlying legitimacy judgments.
realization_criteria: Published or formally acknowledged evidence links fellowship delays to anti-organizing intent or selective discouragement.
At least one authoritative actor or credible external channel treats retaliation as substantiated rather than speculative.

blockers: Leadership may prefer containment and informal fixes.

meta.important_question: Do vulnerable graduate students gain enough protection and visible support to speak more openly?

endpoint_ledger.rationale: Review decisions are a key institutional legitimacy fork distinct from substantive guilt.
realization_criteria: Central administration announces an inquiry, ombuds review, audit, or comparable mechanism with defined scope.
The review is framed as assessing facts or process failures, not merely repeating departmental denial.
endpoint_ledger.status_basis: At T0 administrators deny intent; no meaningful review is yet confirmed.

blockers: Faculty protection, anonymous reporting channels, or broad coalition support could lower participation risk.

meta.important_question: Does the university move from denial to a meaningful independent review or only offer procedural reassurance?

endpoint_ledger.rationale: The scenario explicitly centers public-private belief gaps and dependency-driven silence.
realization_criteria: Visa-dependent or otherwise vulnerable students continue low public participation across multiple ticks despite ongoing grievance.
Union activity relies mostly on indirect or lower-risk participants rather than visible testimony from the most affected cohort.
endpoint_ledger.status_basis: T0 already shows high fear of isolation and strong dependency among visa-dependent students.

blockers: New documents, faculty intervention, or visible student hardship can reactivate attention.
A misstep in official messaging can create a new hook.
endpoint_ledger.contradiction_notes: Temporary dips in visibility do not realize this endpoint if later evidence reignites the story.
endpoint_ledger.description: The controversy remains localized and loses momentum before broader campus or external accountability forms.
endpoint_ledger.label: Issue attention decays

meta.important_question: Does the controversy expand into a broader campus or local media legitimacy issue, or does attention decay?

endpoint_ledger.rationale: Attention decay is a major pressure in campus legitimacy disputes with ambiguous facts.
realization_criteria: No sustained follow-up coverage or broad campus mobilization materializes within the early horizon.
Public discussion volume and coalition expansion decline while official framing stabilizes.
endpoint_ledger.status_basis: Local media attention is limited and broader campus attention is low at T0.

risk_flags.description: The scenario does not establish whether delays are intentional retaliation, routine dysfunction, or mixed causes.
Visa and funding dependence may suppress truthful public reporting and distort visible sentiment.
Observed public calm may understate private grievance, making surface legitimacy measures unreliable.
Population counts are inferred for simulation coherence and may not match the source institution.
Low media bandwidth can cause major evidentiary developments to remain socially under-amplified at T0.

simulation_brief.summary: A graduate student union alleges that a university department is using fellowship payment delays to discourage union organizing. Graduate students show anger but many face visa and funding dependency. Faculty are privately sympathetic but publicly cautious. Administrators deny retaliatory intent. Local media attention exists but is limited. T0 should emphasize public-private belief gaps, fear of isolation, dependency relations, and legitimacy-sensitive reporting questions.
uncertainty_notes: No specific university, department, union local, or administrator identities are provided.
No confirmed evidence at T0 establishes whether fellowship delays are intentional retaliation, routine bureaucracy, or mixed causes.
Media salience and student participation scale are described qualitatively, not quantitatively.

sociology_baseline.description: Private suspicion and sympathy exceed public expression due to dependency and reputational caution.
High silence pressure among vulnerable students and cautious faculty suppresses overt dissent.
Actors are most persuaded by evidence from trusted peers, faculty, or documented cases rather than abstract claims.
Visible participation likely remains low until enough peers act or protective structures emerge.
Information and confidence travel through status-similar student and faculty subnets.
Students need repeated reinforcement from peers, faculty, or media before escalating publicly.
Union and administration frame the issue through competing identity lenses of worker vulnerability versus procedural legitimacy.
Absent new evidence or visible confrontation, outside attention will fade quickly.

sociology_prompt_influences.description: Material and status dependence raises self-censorship and lowers overt participation.
Quiet faculty support can stabilize student beliefs without immediately increasing public speech.
Official denials and process language can slow coalition growth when evidence remains ambiguous.
Outside audiences require concise, documentable hooks before sustaining attention.
